text.en: By about 600 BCE, northern India had both monarchical states (rājyas) and republican states (gaṇas or saṁghas).
All the states of northern India at this time were ruled by kings.
A gaṇa, also called a saṁgha, was a republican state.

explanation.en: By about 600 BCE, the political landscape of northern India included different forms of organisation: monarchical states (rājyas) and republican states (gaṇas or saṁghas). So not every state was ruled by a king.

hints.en: How many forms of state were there in northern India at this time?
Rājya and gaṇa are two different forms.
